description:
SECTION: Contract underspecification

CONTRACT RISK
A family of fields across chat-types carry spec-enumerated wire
vocabularies but are typed as plain String / Vec<String> with no doc
pointer to the enumeration. Callers cannot get compiler-checked
identifiers, IDE completion, or exhaustive-match safety:

  src/chat.rs    SpaceRole.permissions: Vec<String>          (perm names)
  src/chat.rs    ChannelPermission.target_type: String       (kind tag)
  src/chat.rs    ChannelPermission.allow: Vec<String>        (perm names)
  src/chat.rs    ChannelPermission.deny:  Vec<String>        (perm names)
  src/chat.rs    ChatMember.role: String                     (role name)
  src/space_set.rs  RolePatch.permissions: Option<Vec<String>>   (perm names)
  src/ephemeral.rs  ChatStreamEnable.data_types: Vec<String>     (stream-tag names)

Each one has spec-defined valid values
(draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.9, §4.12, §4.15;
 draft-atwood-jmap-chat-wss-00 §7.1). The test code in space_set.rs
and chat.rs uses values like "chat:read", "chat:write",
"send_message", "manage_channels", "ban", "role" — clearly drawn from
an enumeration.

This is the same pattern flagged by the mode prompt for two narrow
fields:
  - JMAP-ly0n.11: ChatPushConfig.urgency + mention_urgency
  - JMAP-ly0n.3:  ChatPresenceEvent.presence
  - JMAP-ly0n.4:  ChatTypingEvent.sender_id

…but those findings did not cover the permission/role/data-type
fields above. This is the systemic API-contract pattern: the crate
has a perfectly good idiom (impl_string_enum! macro used by
DeliveryState, ReadDisposition, ChatKind, Presence) but does not
apply it to permission vocabularies.

WHAT BREAKS FOR CALLERS
- Typos in permission names ("send_messages" vs "send_message") are
  not compile errors; they silently produce inert permission entries
  that the server will likely 4xx but the caller cannot easily catch
  with unit tests.
- Refactoring callers that store a "permission vocabulary cache"
  cannot use Rust's type system to enforce vocabulary correctness.
- IDE / rust-analyzer cannot suggest valid values.
- Cross-crate consumers (jmap-chat-client, jmap-chat-server,
  jmap-testjig) end up duplicating const &str arrays as their own
  vocabulary canon — the type crate should be that canon.

The doc strings give zero contract: "The `allow` property
(draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.15)" tells callers to read the spec.
That's an underspecified contract.

WHY NOT FIX TODAY
The fields are on the wire as JSON strings, so the typed enum needs an
Other(String) catch-all per workspace extras policy. The macro
infrastructure (impl_string_enum!) exists. The blocker is that the
type-crate AGENTS.md says "field names must match spec drafts
exactly" — the typed-enum approach would still serialise to the same
strings, so this is purely a Rust-side type-safety win without a
wire-format change. There is no design tension preventing the
conversion.

RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION
Two options, in order of preference:

(a) Define typed enums backed by impl_string_enum! for each
    vocabulary: ChatPermission, ChannelPermissionTargetType,
    ChatMemberRole, EphemeralStreamDataType. Mirror the existing
    DeliveryState / ReadDisposition / ChatKind shape including an
    Other(String) catch-all per workspace extras policy.

(b) If (a) is judged premature pending draft-01 stabilisation, at
    minimum: add a doc line on each affected field pointing to the
    spec section that enumerates the valid values AND reference an
    associated module-level const &[&str] listing the currently
    spec-known values for caller-side validation.

ORACLE
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.9, §4.12, §4.15; existing
impl_string_enum! usage in chat-types for DeliveryState,
ReadDisposition, ChatKind, Presence; workspace extras-preservation
policy for "wire-format result string enums".
title: Permission/role/data-type vocabulary fields are stringly-typed without spec-enum reference in docs
